messages:
anya: noticed allocator backlog in eu-west1, dozens of GPU pods Pending. ctrl-manager logs show repeated leadership drops.

infra-bot: [ALERT] kube_controller_manager_leader_lost (eu-west1) at 2024-02-14T08:20:34Z

lee: grabbing ctrlmgr logs: `E02 08:19:58 controller_leader.go:88] error renewing lease: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded` then `I02 08:20:15 leaderelection: became leader` then lost again ~30s later.

prateek: any network noise? NAT gateway metrics?

nat-gw: nf_conntrack_count=64980 nf_conntrack_max=65536 tcp_open_rate spike 120k/s at 08:19:50

anya: that math lines up. short-lived outbound connections from an inference job created NAT entries faster than GC. etcd grpcs started failing intermittently.

lee: quick mitigation: increase kube-controller-manager lease time so leader flips stop during the burst. applying patch (small change)

prateek: also increase conntrack on NAT hosts as emergency headroom: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=131072` rolling to 3 hosts now.

infra-bot: deploy status: kube-controller-manager patched, rollout underway.

anya: after the sysctl and patch, leader losses drop to zero and allocator drains backlog over ~2 minutes.

lee: long term: 1) add alert for conntrack utilization and new-entry rate, 2) work with product to reduce ephemeral connection fanout (connection pooling), 3) consider dedicated NAT capacity for GPU regions (cost impact).

prateek: I'll open infra ticket and add cost estimate for extra NAT IPs vs engineering work to pool connections.

anya: ops runbook note: when ctrlmgr leader flips correlate with etcd grpc errors -> inspect NAT conntrack on egress gateways. If >90% consider temporary nf_conntrack_max bump and schedule NAT capacity increase.

infra-bot: cluster health returned to normal at 2024-02-14T08:24:00Z.
